stem.text: A cell of constant electromotive force drives a current $I$ through an external resistor of resistance $R$. The terminal potential difference (p.d.) across the cell is $V$.

stem.alt: Circuit diagram: a dashed box labelled cell contains a cell symbol in series with an internal resistor labelled r; a double-headed arrow labelled V spans the cell; the external circuit has a current arrow labelled I and a resistor labelled R.

stem.text: When the internal resistance $r$ of the cell increases, what is the effect on $V$ and on $I$?
